description.summary: pictures of windows that are not on screen

protocol.description:
A minimised window is, to a taskbar, a name in a list. This protocol lets the compositor hand out a small picture of one instead, so that a stage strip can show what a window looked like when it was hidden rather than asking the user to remember which of four terminals they wanted back.
It is deliberately not a screen-capture protocol. There is no region, no cursor, no damage, no stream, and no way to ask for the current contents of anything. A client can obtain exactly one thing: a downscaled still of a window that the compositor has already decided to hide, at a size the compositor chose. That is enough to draw a stage and not enough to build a screen recorder on, which is the whole point of it being a separate interface from wlr-screencopy rather than a mode of it.
The pictures travel as file descriptors because they do not fit in a Wayland message: a 256x144 image is about 147 kB and libwayland's connection buffer is 4 kB. The compositor seals the memory before sending it, so a client cannot alter a picture another client is also reading.
Warning! This protocol is HadalOS-specific and carries no stability promise. It is versioned so that it can change, not so that it will not.

interface.name: hadal_stage_manager_v1
interface.description: The entry point. A client binds this, and then asks for a thumbnail object per window it wants pictures of.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Thumbnail objects created by this manager are unaffected and must be destroyed separately. Tearing down a taskbar therefore does not have to get the order right.

request.name: watch

description.summary: ask for pictures of one window

request.description:
Creates an object that reports thumbnails of the given window for as long as it lives.
Windows are named by their zwlr_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1, and not by a number of this protocol's own, because a client that already draws a taskbar already has that object and any second identifier would be one more thing that can disagree with the window list.
If a thumbnail already exists when this is called, it is sent immediately; there is no request to poll for one. If the window is not currently hidden, nothing is sent until it is.
Calling this twice for the same toplevel is allowed and yields two independent objects, each of which gets its own copy of the events.

interface.name: hadal_stage_thumbnail_v1
interface.description:
Sends an image event whenever the compositor has a new picture of the window, and a cleared event when it no longer has one — which is what happens when the window is restored, since a picture of how it used to look is worse than no picture at all.
The object outlives the window. When the window closes, the compositor sends cleared and then says nothing further; the client destroys the object at its convenience. Nothing here becomes invalid on its own, because an object that dies when a window does would make every use of it a race against a close the client has not been told about yet.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Any file descriptor already received stays valid and stays the client's to close.

event.name: image
event.description:
A read-only, size-sealed file descriptor holding height * stride bytes of pixel data. The client should mmap it PROT_READ, MAP_PRIVATE.
The descriptor is the client's from the moment it arrives: the client closes it, and must do so, since a taskbar that leaks one per minimise runs out of descriptors in an afternoon.
Each image event supersedes the last. A client holding a mapping from a previous event should drop it, since the compositor has stopped maintaining any relationship between that picture and the window.
Dimensions are chosen by the compositor and are not negotiable. They preserve the window's aspect ratio and are bounded on the long edge, so a client must scale to whatever box it draws in and must not assume a constant size across events — a window that is resized while hidden produces a differently shaped picture next time.

event.name: cleared

description.summary: there is no longer a picture

event.description:
The compositor has discarded its thumbnail of this window. Sent when the window is restored or closed.
A client that keeps drawing the last image it received after this will show a picture of a window that is on screen and looks different, which is worse than showing nothing.

enum.name: format
enum.description: One entry, and a named enum rather than a bare uint, because the alternative is a protocol whose format is implicit and therefore undocumented. Adding a second entry is a version bump.

entry.name: abgr8888
entry.summary: 8-bit RGBA, little-endian, alpha last in memory; premultiplied
